stem: A meter passes calibration but repeatedly fails verification later in the shift. What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: Measurement control is unstable and the device/process requires investigation before results are trusted
Passing calibration once proves every later reading is valid
Verification failures can be ignored if the display looks reasonable
The crop should be adjusted instead of checking the instrument
rationale: Calibration and verification serve different purposes. Repeated verification failure indicates measurement quality is not under control.
